items.claim: The fallback `(( ! $+functions[compdef] ))` still runs `_rg "$@"` when the script is sourced before `compinit`, so the failure from issue #2956 persists in that ordering.
items.consequence: A .zshrc with `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` placed above `autoload -Uz compinit; compinit` (or with no compinit at all): compdef is undefined, so `_rg` runs outside a completion context. Reproduced in zsh 5.9: prints `_rg:341: command not found: _arguments`, returns status 1 on every shell start, and no completion is registered for rg.

items.claim: The hard-coded `$funcstack[1] == _rg` check misfires when the file is autoloaded under any other name, so the first completion attempt returns nothing.
items.consequence: The generated script is installed in fpath as `_ripgrep` (the `#compdef rg` tag makes compinit bind rg to `_ripgrep`). On the first `rg --<TAB>`, funcstack[1] is `_ripgrep` and compdef exists, so the else branch runs `compdef _rg rg` and no matches are produced. Reproduced with a stubbed `_arguments`: TAB #1 never calls it, TAB #2 does. Before this change the first TAB worked.

items.claim: Sourcing the file by the bare relative name `_rg` sets `funcstack[1]` to `_rg`, so the script wrongly takes the "being autoloaded" branch.
items.consequence: After compinit, `cd ~/.zsh-complete && source _rg` (or `. _rg` resolved via PATH): funcstack[1] is the literal `_rg`, so `_rg "$@"` runs. Reproduced: `_arguments:comparguments:327: can only be called from completion function`, status 1, rg completion not registered. `source ./_rg` works, so the behaviour depends on how the path is spelled.

items.claim: The FAQ presents the `source <(...)` line as a drop-in .zshrc addition without saying it must come after `compinit`.
items.consequence: A reader with no compinit call, or who pastes the line near the top of .zshrc, gets `command not found: _arguments` on every shell start and no completions. The FAQ describes this method as the easier one and gives no hint about ordering.

items.claim: The snippet the reader is told to add to `$HOME/.zshrc` begins with a `$ ` prompt marker, unlike the `fpath=` snippet just above it.
items.consequence: A user copies the line verbatim into .zshrc as instructed; zsh then tries to run a command named `$` and reports `command not found: $` at every startup, and completions never load.

items.claim: The recommended fpath instructions do not say the `fpath=(...)` line must precede `compinit`, so they can still silently do nothing.
items.consequence: A user appends `fpath=($HOME/.zsh-complete $fpath)` to the end of .zshrc, after their framework or their own `compinit` call. compinit has already scanned fpath, `_rg` is never registered, and rg gets only default file completion with no error.

items.claim: The `! $+functions[compdef]` clause exists only so `ci/test-complete` can source the file, which couples production behaviour to the test and makes the test depend on compdef being absent.
items.consequence: If `ci/test-complete` runs in a zsh where compdef is defined (for example a `.zshenv` that runs compinit), the sourced file takes the else branch and prints no specs. Reproduced in simulation: 341 spec lines without compdef, 0 with it, so the script aborts with `Failed to get comp_args`. Keying the dump path off `_RG_COMPLETE_LIST_ARGS` would fix both this and the before-compinit error.

items.claim: The new top-level check uses zsh-native subscripts and runs under the user's own shell options when sourced, so it errors under `setopt ksh_arrays`.
items.consequence: A .zshrc with `setopt ksh_arrays` followed by `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`: reproduced, prints `/proc/self/fd/13:441: bad output format specification` on every shell start. Registration still succeeds only because the arithmetic error happens to fall through to the else branch.

items.claim: The new note is ungrammatical: the clause is missing its subject ("is generally slower") and uses "setup" as a verb.
items.consequence: The sentence reads "while this approach is easier to setup, is generally slower than the previous method"; it should read "easier to set up, it is generally slower".

items.claim: The man page's SHELL COMPLETION section still documents only the fpath method, so it now disagrees with the FAQ.
items.consequence: A user reading `man rg` sees only "move _rg to one of your $fpath directories" and never learns that the generated script can be sourced directly, which is the feature this PR adds.
